change_2_gain_ratio.arithmetic_reasoning: Operative code (render.py): music_gain_db_for_ratio computes target = voice_lufs + 10*log10(ratio), then gain_db = target - music_lufs, clamped to [MUSIC_GAIN_MIN_DB=-60, MUSIC_GAIN_MAX_DB=+24]; resolve_music_volume converts that dB gain to a LINEAR AMPLITUDE multiplier via 10**(gain_db/20) and applies it through ffmpeg volume=. Worked math: OLD ratio 0.30 -> offset 10*log10(0.30) = -5.2288 dB, so at voice -20 LUFS the music target is -25.23 LUFS. IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY FOUND AND DOCUMENTED: the existing code comments claim the 0.30 offset is '-10.46 dB', but -10.46 dB = 20*log10(0.30), NOT the 10*log10(0.30) = -5.23 dB the code actually computes; the pre-existing comment block was stale/wrong and was corrected alongside the constant per the contract's no-stale-docs rule. Three interpretations considered: (A) halve the ratio to 0.15 -> offset 10*log10(0.15) = -8.2391 dB; at voice -20 LUFS music target -28.24 LUFS, i.e. music exactly 3.0103 dB QUIETER than the 0.30 target at every measurement pair (10*log10(0.15)-10*log10(0.30) = -3.0103 dB). This directly implements 'voice counts double while music's absolute target logic is unchanged' and is monotone with the operator's 'background music is too much' complaint. (B) literal '0.3 to 2' -> ratio 2.0 -> offset +3.0103 dB, music LOUDER than voice; REJECTED as the exact opposite of the stated goal. (C) perceptual/sone reading of 'vocals at 200%' (Stevens' law: doubling PERCEIVED loudness needs ~+10 LU) with the voice path fixed at unity would require cutting the music target by 10 dB -> ratio 0.030; REJECTED as over-aggressive: a 10 dB drop risks burying the bed under narration and the previous gain-clamp fix already tightened the bed once, so a measured ~3 dB step is the conservative, directly-traceable change. CHOSEN: new ratio 0.15, implemented in commit a4c0a6d. The direction was sanity-checked against the formula itself: a SMALLER ratio produces a MORE NEGATIVE offset (log10 is monotone increasing), i.e. the music target sits further BELOW voice_lufs = quieter; 0.15 < 0.30 therefore strictly reduces music loudness relative to voice for every (voice_lufs, music_lufs) pair, and a dedicated regression test (test_new_ratio_is_quieter_than_old_030_for_same_inputs) proves the exact -3.0103 dB delta across four measurement pairs. Gain-bounds re-verification with the new -8.24 dB offset: worst physically possible cut = -23 LUFS vocals - 8.24 dB offset - (+3 LUFS music, full-scale-square-wave physical ceiling) = -34.24 dB; MUSIC_GAIN_MIN_DB=-60 leaves 25.76 dB of headroom beyond even that impossible edge, so no real upload is ever clamped away from the exact 0.15 target. Boost side: ceiling +24 dB covers music down to -48.24 LUFS under -16 LUFS vocals. CONCLUSION: -60/+24 remain correctly calibrated for ratio 0.15; bounds unchanged.

(The pre-existing '-10.46 dB' figure in comments was 20*log10(0.30), not what the code computed; corrected in this change.)
